purpose: Reviewer-facing build and compiler-cache cost audit; no further compilation was performed for this report.

original_github_ci.measurement: Ninja first completed compile at16:38:01.090725 to last link17:05:30.199121 Debug; Release12:54:23.547245 to13:21:29.909060. original_github_ci.cache_interpretation: Debug cache arrived already at953MB and ended at99.34% with112cleanup passes. Saturation supports increasing its capacity; legitimate header invalidations also cause misses, so112cleanups do not explain every miss.

other_cost_detail.method: Intervals from original timestamped job log, not full step accounting. Container, ccache installation/restore/save and artifact upload intervals are disjoint; the residual includes checkout and remaining small transitions.

local_completed_command_snapshots.interpretation: Latest completed command for each output across recorded incremental invocations; elapsed commands overlap and include ccache, compiler and filesystem time. This is not a clean-build wall-time comparison.

local_build_matrix.original_github_each_job_mode: One variant only: Debug or Release
local_build_matrix.comparison_warning: Do not compare the dual-variant local command count or walltime with a single-variant GitHub job. Snapshot timings differ in source, compiler, cache state, concurrent node load and build scope.

compiler_phase_attribution.link_command_elapsed: Measured for completed local Ninja executable/shared-library linker rules, deduplicating registry side outputs. GoogleTest commands also include post-link registry discovery; its cost is not separated.
compiler_phase_attribution.reason: No GCC -ftime-report or Clang time traces were collected. The large template headers imply potential work, but no measured stage fraction or speedup is claimed.

cross_checkout_ccache_proof.proof_scope: One real production object, separately for Debug and Release, in two distinct source/build trees with equal layouts, toolchain and options. This proves preprocessed-cache reuse, not direct hits or full-project hit rate.

findings.effect: Addresses observed saturation without reducing test/build scope.
findings.limitation: Larger cache transfer/storage may offset benefits; warm full-run hit rate and net walltime remain to be measured.

findings.change: Remove optional legacy1D archive downloads; configure ENABLE_COUPLED_PROBLEMS=OFF
findings.effect: Avoids downloads and known unsuccessful archive link probes. Compile-only client objects remain enabled, preserving interface compilation.
findings.limitation: This does not claim runtime validation of a compatible optional1D installation.

findings.change: When optional1D is genuinely enabled, depend on its existing application targets instead of compiling duplicate client objects
findings.effect: Avoids duplicate client translation units without omitting ordinary enabled application builds.
Provides evidence for later build-cost work; does not change compiler options or omit targets.
findings.limitation: Latest-output records across incremental runs are not a clean-build baseline, and command elapsed times overlap.

findings.effect: Bounds runtime thread pools; does not set Ninja parallelism, change assertions, or alter Debug optimization flags.

preserved_contracts: Debug and Release remain separate CI jobs.
Debug retains-DDEBUG and-O0; this patch does not silently replace it with Release.
All default application targets and public-header self-containment checks remain in the ordinary ALL build.
GoogleTest aggregation and semantic categories still determine runtime execution; no unvalidated fine-grained C++ selection was enabled.

limitations: Original hosted-runner build cannot be split into per-TU or preprocessing/template/optimizer timings from completion-only console logs.
Local Ninja entries include overlapping work and cache effects; do not sum them as elapsed build walltime.
Optimized ALL build was still active when the snapshot was read; later outputs and final build outcome are not asserted.
Successful local cross-checkout reuse does not prove the 4GB hosted-runner working set is sufficient.
A fresh hosted Debug and Release run is required to measure end-to-end CI improvement.

integrated_candidate_build.build_result: All configured application, library, GoogleTest and public-header targets built successfully in DebugRelease. Optional Coral, external FVM drivers and MetricFlowX package configurations disabled.

incremental_build_cache.interpretation: These changed translation units missed. This is not a warm-cache speedup measurement. Separate equivalent-checkout source-object proof below establishes reusable cache results.

integrated_candidate_build.timing_scope: Latest command per output after initial full build and incremental fixture rebuild. Command times include launcher/compiler/linker/I/O and overlap; they are not a clean-build duration or a hosted-CI comparison.

representative_compiler_stage_probe.execution_policy: Do not execute until root explicitly authorizes after timed CTest completes. Commands execute sequentially, no configuration or source/build-tree mutation.

ccache_log_intervals.note: These are ccache-log event intervals. The real-compiler interval includes assembler and wrapper work beyond the cc1 TOTAL timer; intervals are not all GCC compiler phase timers.

interpretation: The GNU TOTAL and phase rows describe this individual compiler invocation. Subsystem timers such as template instantiation and preprocessing overlap those phases and sometimes one another; do not add phase and subsystem rows together.
GGC is GCC garbage-collected allocation accounting, not resident memory. The external process-time maximum RSS is recorded separately.
External process wall/user/system includes launcher, ccache, preprocessing/hash work, compiler and assembler; GNU time-report timers cover GCC work rather than the entire launcher process.
These forced-recaching diagnostic builds preserve all actual Debug/Release flags and prefix maps, add only timing and isolated dependency/output paths, and do not measure normal cache-hit latency.
The representative final-source local GNU11.4/deal.II9.8 TU is not the original GNU13.3/deal.II9.7.1 hosted CI. No fraction or speedup is extrapolated to other TUs or all CI.
Only source-file SHA is checked directly here; root freezes the relevant C++ source/header tree while these probes execute.

compiler_stage_provenance.path_aliases: Worker source, build, artifact and cache directories are replaced by named placeholders in the published commands; original command/source hashes are preserved.
compiler_stage_provenance.scope: One heavy GoogleTest translation unit in Debug and Release, with diagnostic -ftime-report instrumentation. Timings are not extrapolated to the complete CI or used as a matched Debug/Release speed benchmark.

findings: The action exposes update-package-index and max-size but no archive-compression or extra-package input.
restore.ts installs ccache only when io.which(ccache) finds no existing executable. It installs only ccache via apt-get; it does not install zstd.
The exact locked @actions/cache4.1.0 dependency probes zstd --quiet --version. Empty output selects gzip; available zstd selects ZstdWithoutLong.
On GNU/Linux save then passes tar --use-compress-program zstdmt; extraction uses unzstd. Without zstd it uses tar -z.
The compression method participates in the cache version hash. Installing zstd before restoring cannot reuse the previous gzip-format cache entry, even with the same visible cache key.
safe_candidate: Before ccache-action run one apt-get update followed by apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ccache zstd.
Set ccache-action update-package-index:false. Because ccache is already present, its installer and apt-get update are skipped; only one package-index update occurs.
Verify command -v ccache, zstd --quiet --version and archive command in actual action logs; measure equivalent-size restore/save timings and end-to-end walltime.
cache_archive_followup_not_implemented.migration_warning: Switching archive format invalidates reuse of existing gzip cache version for the first zstd-restoring run. Do not mix this with the4GB capacity experiment and then attribute changed hit rate to capacity alone. A container image including ccache and zstd is an alternative, requiring its own image rollout.
cache_archive_followup_not_implemented.priority: Secondary: current compress+save is about30seconds of a56minute job. Larger4GB caches can make it more relevant, but no zstd speedup has been measured.
